name: library-layer-references
body:
Reference direction across library layers: only a `section` helper call and a `{{ template "<name>" . }}` layout-composition call cross the layer boundary. A local template's `section` helper call resolves against the merged section namespace, so a local template invokes an external section template exactly as it invokes a local one (section-helper). A layout invokes another library layout by its layout name with the standard `{{ template "<name>" . }}` action, resolved against the merged library's layout set — every slide and section layout, whichever layer contributes it — both at render time and at the load-time example check (example-layout-composition, template-language); the invoking layout's own `media` helper still resolves in that layout's own layer. Every other reference written inside a template or theme resolves within that template's or theme's own layer: the layout `media` helper, a `media:` URL, a `theme:<name>/` reference, and a theme's own CSS, layout and media files all resolve inside the layer that owns the referencing template or theme, and each layer's media is served from that layer's own `media/` root. A `section` helper call's child arguments resolve against the merged section namespace like the call's target, and each child's own `media`/`theme:`-based references resolve in that child template's own owning layer (child-constructor). The external layer is a self-contained library: every reference inside an external-layer template or theme resolves within the external library alone, so the external library validates on its own as a standalone library before the merge (templates-dir-validation). A reference from an external template or theme to a section, theme or media name that only the local layer carries is a templates error, as is a reference from a local template or theme to an external theme or media name; a local template's `section` helper call naming an external section resolves.

AC: a local slide template whose layout calls an external section template renders that external section; a local layout's `media` helper argument, a local theme's `media:` reference and a local theme's `theme:<name>/` reference each resolve to a file inside the local layer — its `media/` tree or one of its `themes/<name>/` directories — and a local theme's `theme:<name>/` reference names a theme in that same local layer; a local template or theme that references an external `media/` file, or a local theme whose `theme:<name>/` reference names an external theme, is a templates error; an external template or theme that references a section, theme or media file carried only by the local layer is a templates error naming the external template or theme; a local template's `section` call passing an external-layer child resolves and the child's `media` resolves in the external layer; the external library validates as a standalone library with the local `templates/` directory absent; a layout invoking another library layout by name with `{{ template "<name>" . }}` renders the invoked layout at render time and at the load-time example check, and the invoking layout's `media` still resolves in its own layer.
